title: Model bootstrapping adaptor and certification scan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: What: Implement an end-to-end bootstrapping adaptor that automates weights intake -> standardized conversion -> deterministic smoke certification -> canonical pin creation and publishes a minimal performance profile to the catalog. Why: Current onboarding requires manual handoffs across conversion, profiling, and pinning. This adaptor reduces iteration time for OSS model teams and prevents serving regressions by gating model pins on deterministic certification steps. Scope: prototype adaptor service + CI jobs + a deterministic smoke-suite and telemetry hooks to publish a lightweight profile to the model catalog. Exclusions: full-scale benchmarking and resource-heavy calibration; those remain in separate profiling pipelines.
success_metrics: Median time from weights upload to certified pin < 3 hours for small models (<10B)
Automated smoke-suite pass rate >= 98% for accepted models
Reduction in manual conversion handoffs by 80% in Q2
First-pin rollouts use adaptor recommendations in 90% of onboarding flows
acceptance_criteria: Adaptor accepts a signed weights manifest and produces a converted runtime artifact with reproducible checksums
Deterministic smoke-suite runs in CI and produces stability and perf metrics stored in telemetry
Adaptor creates a canonical pin entry in staging catalog and attaches the minimal performance profile (latency P50/P95 for 32-token and 512-token workloads)
All produced artifacts are signed and provenance metadata is recorded in S3 + catalog entry
E2E integration test that simulates network-constrained routing and validates fallback behavior passes
technical_notes: Intake: webhook based on existing artifact-gateway; consumer validates signed manifest, verifies SHA256 of weight shards
Conversion: run weight-normalizer image (containerized) with deterministic seed, fixed quantization config per model family
Smoke-suite: fixed prompt set (50 short + 10 long), tokenization sanity checks, KV cache warmup, and micro-benchmarks for attention kernels
Cert scan: compare outputs against golden-diff tolerance (top-k token overlap thresholds) and track divergence reason codes
Pin: generate canonical pin object: {model_family, version, runtime-compatible-tags, checksum, profile_id} (store as catalog record)
Telemetry: publish profile metrics to Console ingestion endpoint with token-level cost estimate and inferred batching recommendation
Security: run automated provenance checks and require KMS-wrapped signing key for production pins
decisions: Use deterministic conversion container image to ensure reproducible byte-level artefacts across runs
Adopt a lightweight smoke-suite focused on stability + kernel-level perf (not full benchmark), to keep CI cheap and fast
Pin creation blocked on smoke-suite and signature verification; manual override requires SRE + PM approval logged in audit trail
risks: False negatives from smoke-suite could block acceptable models — mitigation: tune thresholds after initial run and allow temporary canary pins
Non-deterministic conversions due to dependency drift — mitigation: pin base image digests and CI cache layers
Large models (>50B) may time out the adaptor CI — mitigation: fallback to batched offline profiling pipeline and mark pin as pending
